guarantees.claim: In StRandReset when entropy_ready_i is false, st_d remains StRandReset and rand_valid_set is asserted, providing dummy entropy to unblock the application interface without SW.

In StRandReset when entropy_ready_i is true, rand_valid_clear is asserted, mode_latch is asserted, and based on mode_i: for EntropyModeSw seed_en is set and st_d goes to StSwSeedWait; for EntropyModeEdn seed_en is set, timer_update asserted, st_d goes to StRandEdn; for other values st_d goes to StRandErrIncorrectMode.
In StRandReady, timer_enable is forced to 1 and prng_en is initially driven from prng_en_rand_q[0] unless overridden later in the state.

In StRandReady, if (rand_update_i || rand_consumed_i) and ((fast_process_i && in_keyblock_i) || !fast_process_i) is true, prng_en is set to 1, data_update is set to 1; if rand_consumed_i, st_d transitions to StRandGenerate and rand_valid_clear is set; otherwise st_d stays StRandReady.

In StRandReady, when mode_q == EntropyModeEdn and (entropy_refresh_req_i or threshold_hit_q) is true, seed_en is set to 1, st_d transitions to StRandEdn, timer_update is set, and threshold_hit_clr is set.

In StRandEdn, entropy_req is driven by seed_req, timer_enable is set; if timer_expired and non_zero_wait_timer_limit, st_d transitions to StRandErrWaitExpired; else if entropy_req_o && entropy_ack_i, seed_ack is set, and if seed_done st_d transitions to StRandGenerate with prng_en, data_update, rand_valid_clear under the fast_process/in_keyblock condition, otherwise stays StRandEdn; if rand_update_i/rand_consumed_i occurs during wait, prng_en=1, data_update=1, rand_valid_clear = rand_consumed_i, and stays in StRandEdn.
In StSwSeedWait, seed_ack = seed_req & seed_update_i; if seed_done, st_d transitions to StRandGenerate with prng_en=1, data_update=1, rand_valid_clear=1; otherwise stays StSwSeedWait.
In StRandGenerate, aux_update=1, rand_valid_set=1, prng_en=prng_en_rand_q[0], and st_d transitions to StRandReady.
In StRandErrWaitExpired, st_d goes to StRandErr and err_o is driven with valid=1, code=ErrWaitTimerExpired, info=timer_value.
In StRandErrIncorrectMode, st_d goes to StRandErr and err_o is driven with valid=1, code=ErrIncorrectEntropyMode, info=mode_q.

In StRandErr, rand_valid_set=1, prng_en = (rand_update_i | rand_consumed_i) & ((fast_process_i & in_keyblock_i) | ~fast_process_i); data_update = prng_en; if err_processed_i, st_d goes to StRandReset; else stays StRandErr.
In StTerminalError, st_d remains StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o is set to 1.
If the current state is not any defined state (invalid sparse encoding), st_d is forced to StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o is set.
guarantees.cond: st not matching any named state

guarantees.claim: After the case statement, if lc_escalate_en_i asserts (life cycle escalation), st_d is unconditionally driven to StTerminalError, overriding any normal FSM transition.

assumptions.claim: entropy_ready_i must eventually assert after SW has configured KMAC; while false, dummy entropy is continuously provided but the FSM will never leave StRandReset.
assumptions.risk: Permanent deadlock in reset with dummy entropy if SW never signals ready.

assumptions.claim: When entropy_ready_i is true, mode_i must be a valid entropy mode (EntropyModeSw or EntropyModeEdn); any other value immediately triggers StRandErrIncorrectMode.
assumptions.risk: FSM enters error state before any entropy processing, blocking normal operation.

assumptions.claim: The parameter non_zero_wait_timer_limit must reflect whether the wait timer has a non‑zero limit; if it is zero, the timer expiration in StRandEdn will never trigger StRandErrWaitExpired, potentially leaving the FSM waiting indefinitely for an EDN response.
assumptions.risk: Indefinite hang if EDN never responds and timer is effectively disabled.

assumptions.claim: seed_req must accurately reflect the PRNG primitive’s reseed request, as entropy_req directly forwards it to the EDN interface.
assumptions.risk: Missing or spurious EDN requests, causing either starvation or unnecessary reseeds.

assumptions.claim: err_processed_i must be asserted by external logic to transition out of StRandErr; otherwise the FSM remains in error while still providing entropy, which may be acceptable but could stall higher‑level recovery.
assumptions.risk: Stuck in error state indefinitely if the error handler never acknowledges.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en_i must correctly represent a life‑cycle escalation; if spuriously asserted, the FSM enters StTerminalError permanently with sparse_fsm_error_o set, causing a denial of service.
assumptions.risk: Unrecoverable terminal error and possible system halt.

assumptions.claim: fast_process_i and in_keyblock_i must be consistent with the actual hashing context; the condition (fast_process_i && in_keyblock_i) gates random expansion, and an incorrect combination can suppress needed entropy refresh.
assumptions.risk: Stale randomness reused in fast‑process non‑keyblock scenarios, weakening masking.

uncertain_points.claim: In StRandEdn, if a new rand_update or rand_consumed event occurs while waiting for an EDN response, the FSM handles the request but does not reset the wait timer. The timer can expire while the new operation is still in progress, causing a spurious transition to StRandErrWaitExpired and then StRandErr, even though the entropy request is still being served.
uncertain_points.cond: st == StRandEdn, (rand_update_i || rand_consumed_i) true, and timer_expired later
uncertain_points.risk: Erroneous error state during legitimate operation, potentially interrupting hash processing and disclosing error information.

uncertain_points.claim: The condition (fast_process_i && in_keyblock_i) appears in the entropy consumption logic to prevent expansion when fast_process is active unless a key block is being processed. The reason for requiring in_keyblock_i in this security‑critical path is not clear from RTL alone; it may be safe, but if in_keyblock_i is incorrectly de‑asserted, fresh entropy is never provided, leaving potentially stale or repeated randomness.
uncertain_points.risk: Silent re‑use of old entropy, undermining masking/randomness guarantees.

uncertain_points.claim: threshold_hit_q is only examined in StRandReady for reseeding and only when mode_q == EntropyModeEdn. If threshold_hit_q can assert in other states or modes, it would be ignored, possibly missing a needed entropy refresh.
uncertain_points.risk: Stale entropy not refreshed as intended, weakening security.
